findings.reason: a node dispatched on §13 will remove the scan, re-measure the served read, and find it still outside the 30 s deadline with no declared second lever, so the section either blocks or the node invents a change beyond its brief; the mechanism needs to name what else the served path spends (the `_live_sessions` → `crew/directory.directory()` call it never mentions is the obvious candidate) or the deadline needs a figure the cited evidence actually supports.
findings.text: §13 says the resolver "walks every row: the aggregate's rows, which §11 left unbounded … For a review row that resolution calls `_reviewed_run_id` with every row, which copies the list and scans it", and treats that scan as the cost of the served read; but §11's probe at `reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py:256` with `pointers=[]` reads the identical aggregate rows and runs the identical `_plan_of_run` → `_reviewed_run` → `_reviewed_run_id(source, list(rows.values()))` path for the identical review rows, and answered in 5.7 s, while `reckon/roadmap.py:3421-3423` memoises the resolver to one call per roadmap build, so the served read pays that scan once too — the plan's own two measurements therefore bound the scan well under 6 s and leave ~40 s of the 45 s unexplained, with no other cost named

response_events.note: §13 is rewritten to profile the served roadmap read on reckon with live pointers before changing code, and to remove the stage the profile names; the quadratic scan is kept only as one candidate, not the stated cause.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py:299` resolves each row's plan before the window check at `:303`, `:140` passes `list(rows.values())` into `dispatch_sessions._reviewed_run_id`, `reckon/ledger.py:1764-1767` bounds only the per-run documents and leaves the aggregate unbounded, and `a-project-reads-as-one-picture` §8 carries the 45 s re-measure the section cites.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every assertion in §13 fails at its base arm (the quadratic scan, the coordinator equality on a fixture with a long-queued row and in-window review pointers, and the served read), and the fixture carries the discriminating cases rather than only the easy ones.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the fragment §13 names is the plan's own `docs/evidence/fragments/a-coordinator-sees-the-board/` directory, which is durable, in-repo, and already holds ten landed sections' fragments, though the section itself names no filename.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §13 introduces no symbol, file or comment carrying a section label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §13 blames the >45 s served read on a quadratic review-subject scan, but that same scan runs in §11's 5.7 s probe over the same aggregate rows, so the plan names no mechanism for the ~40 s it has to remove.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 carries one deliverable, the resolver's review-subject resolution made cheap, and its three assertions all measure that one thing.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §13's code builds on §2 and §11, both declared done and landed on main (`resolve_plan_coordinators`, `run_rows_from_documents(modified_since=…)`), and the section that waits on it declares the relationship on its own side (`a-project-reads-as-one-picture` §8 now waits on `a-coordinator-sees-the-board` §13), so no missing `depends-on` entry can starve the node.
